speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Imports and exports are not separately recorded.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: It merely binds the present rate.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: No; it is a reduction in duty. It is dutiable under the present tariff at 174 per cent, forty per cent and forty per cent. The new rate is 274 Per cent.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
Customs tariff-124.	Oysters, shelled, in
bulk, 5 cents per gallon.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This is a reduction. The former rates were seven cents under the British preference, nine cents under the intermediate and ten cents per gallon under the general tariff. Under this item New Zealand has by virtue of her trade agreement a fixed rate of five cents per gallon, but with no guaranteed margins of preference.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: What is the United States duty against our shelled oysters?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Free.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: The whole year?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
They have agreed to
bind the free entry presently accorded to oysters.

What quantity of
oysters do we import from the United States?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
In bulk, shelled, 105,000
gallons, valued at $162,000 in 1935.

Personally I should
like to see an absolute embargo on the entry into Canada of the bluepoint so-called oyster, not because of competition-I am not afraid of competition-but because they are a misrepresentation and a fraud upon our famous Buctouche and Aldouane oysters. They are really not oysters at all. They do not taste *like oysters. They look more like quahaugs or clams, and when people eat them they say, "If those are oysters we won't buy any more." They are therefore injurious to our Buctouche and Al'diouane oysters.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.

. Canada-U.S. Trade Agreement
Customs tariff-ex 133. Lobsters, fresb, free.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: This is a reduction. The present duties are fifteen per cent under the British, twenty per cent under the intermediate and twenty-five per cent under the general tariff.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext:
Do we get free entry
for lobsters?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: We get free entry for Canadian lobsters.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: What was the rate?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: They are free. We imported from the United States last year fifty pounds of fresh lobsters, valued at $15, and we exported to the United States 99,000 hundredweight, valued at $1,629,000.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext:
Is not this the issue?
Why should we have done this if we do not expect the Americans to do some more trading in lobsters in our market? There is no purpose at all.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The purpose is to ensure the continuance of the free entry of our lobsters into the United States for three years.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext:
Although they did most
of the buying last year. We bought only a trifling quantity from them.

How long have we had
the right of free entry into the United States?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
I cannot answer that
offhand.

This is most important,
because the United States could get deep sea lobsters from Bermuda and other places. They encourage our trade and they should be given consideration therefor.

Is it not a fact that very
few lobsters are caught in the United States?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: That is right.
The maritimes and Newfoundland are the main sources of supply. The United States want our lobsters.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
Yes; and if they want
free entry, what is the matter?

They have nothing to
enter.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext:
Item agreed to.
Customs tariff-ex 133. Scallops, fresh but not frozen, free.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
This is a reduction.
Scallops are at present dutiable, fifteen per cent under the British preference, twenty per cent under the intermediate and twenty-five per cent under the general tariff. Under schedule II the United States guarantee the free entry of Canadian scallops, fresh but not frozen, the product of Canada. Our exports to the United States last year were 584,000 pounds, valued at $103,000.

What were our imports
of scallops for the same period?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The imports are not separately recorded; they are included in a bulk item.
From what countries do we get them?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: We do not.
No imports?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Nothing to speak of.

speakerposition: stagedirection
speechtext: Item agreed to.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I think we have made fair progress and I move that the committee rise, report progress and ask leave to sit again.

speakerposition: Leader of the Official Opposition
speechtext: Will the minister be prepared to give us evidence of values and information of that kind in connection with the next item?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
I shall try to be as fully prepared as possible.
Progress reported.
On motion of Mr. Mackenzie King the house adjourned at 10.55 p.m.
